## D.1 — Self-trained model; training in Python, inference in C 🔒
`D-004` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden (confirmed with instructor) · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

A locally-trained, self-authored model is permitted; hosted APIs and third-party
pretrained weights are not. Therefore: training in `tools/train/`, weights versioned under
`models/` with the training commit in the header, **inference in C in `src/analysis/`**, no
network at runtime.

**Why inference in C.** First and most important for the grade: the runtime path sits
inside the supervised multi-process architecture, and a Python process there muddies the
boundary a grader must verify in sixty seconds. Second: it removes an interpreter, a
garbage collector and ~30 MB of RSS from a 48-hour memory-stability test we are graded on.

**What the model is not doing.** The features are the intelligence — operating-point
binning, per-bin baselines, Mahalanobis residuals, Theil–Sen trends, all hand-written.
Delete the weights file and the system still produces residuals and trends; it loses only
the final labeling step. That separation is deliberate and it is the answer at the defense.

## D.2 — Analysis pipeline shape 🔒
Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

Operating-point binning (RPM × load × coolant temp) → per-bin running mean/variance →
multivariate residual (Mahalanobis) → robust trend (Theil–Sen) → classifier → state
machine with hysteresis and dwell.

**Why binning comes first.** Comparing a cold idle to a warm cruise is a false-alarm
generator. Every comparison happens inside one bin, against genuinely comparable
conditions. This single step removes more false positives than anything else downstream.

**Why multivariate.** The signal is the *correlation between sensors*, not any single
sensor's value — oil pressure is supposed to rise with RPM. A measure of anomaly that
already accounts for normal partnerships, and alarms only when a partnership breaks, is
what makes this something a threshold provably cannot do (handout §3.3).

Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

No verdict reaches the user until it has persisted. Trip and un-trip levels differ
deliberately.

**Why.** A monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged, and an unplugged monitor is worse
than none because someone far away believes it is on duty. **False-positive rate is a
first-class metric in `docs/EVALUATION.md`, not an afterthought.**

## D.4 — The threshold test, as a standing rule 🔒
Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

Every diagnostic we ship must require at least two cooperating sensors to reach its
conclusion. If a single threshold on a single value could produce the verdict, it is not
intelligence and it does not count. **Write the reason down in `docs/DESIGN.md` when adding a
diagnostic** — this is checked at the defense.

  within a minute.
- **Cooling** — partially block radiator airflow with cardboard.
- **Sensor fault** — unplug a sensor. Also demo day's injected fault, so it gets rehearsed.
- **Oil** — log continuously across a real oil change on both vehicles. Cannot be faked
  and cannot be rushed, which is why baseline collection starts at M2.

Ten labeled recordings we made beat ten thousand unlabeled samples we found, because we
know what ours mean — and we will be asked at the defense how we know.

## E.3 — 48-hour soak: live sensors vs. synthetic CAN ❓ OPEN
`D-006` · **Owner:** Camden · **Tracked as:** GitHub issue (label `decision`, milestone M4)
· **Must close before M4** · Blocks nothing before M3

**The conflict.** Our PC-side rig generating CAN traffic is a good idea and we are building
it regardless — handout §5 explicitly endorses a replay harness as "a legitimate systems
artifact." But the same paragraph says: *"The 48-hour soak and the live demonstration run
on live sensors; everything else may run on honest replay."* A soak on generated traffic is
synthesized data by definition.

**Options.** (a) Written exception from Pallickara — email drafted at
`docs/professor-email-draft.md`. (b) Add MPU-6050 + DS18B20 (~$8) so the soak runs on
genuinely live sensors while CAN is replayed and labeled; bonus is vibration order-tracked
against CAN RPM, which no dongle can produce. (c) Soak in the parked car on live CAN with a
battery tender.

**Posture.** Build as if (a) is refused. (b) is the default fallback and the tree is already
shaped for it — `src/capture/` exists and is empty on purpose. The `src=` field is in the
record format regardless.

---

# F. Process, team and tooling

## F.1 — Git and pull-request law 🔒
Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

The binding ruleset lives in **`CLAUDE.md` §7**, because that is the file the agent reads
every session. Summary of the load-bearing parts:

- Claude never commits to `main`, never merges, never force-pushes, never `git add -A`.
- One commit = one idea. **≤ 150 changed lines and ≤ 3 files**, default one file.
- One PR = one reviewable claim. **≤ 500 changed lines, ≤ 10 commits.**
- **If the reviewer does not understand a line, the PR does not merge.** The remedy is
  explanation or a smaller commit, never trust.
- Every commit builds and passes tests on its own.

**Why so strict.** Our process grade is computed from transcripts corroborated against
commits, the git history is a graded deliverable, and neither of us will break down a
thousand-line diff. A commit small enough to review in ninety seconds is a commit we will
actually review — and the defense asks us to answer for individual lines.

## F.2 — Ownership map 🔒
Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

| Owner | Subsystems |
|---|---|
| **Camden** | `src/can/`, `src/capture/`, `src/ipc/`, `drivers/` |
| **Lance** | `src/store/`, `src/analysis/`, `tools/train/` |
| **Shared** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/interface/`, `src/common/`, build, docs |

Ownership means **first authorship and answerability at the defense**, not exclusivity.
Each partner must still be able to answer one question from across the boundary — demo day
guarantees one.

## F.3 — Milestone dates ❓ OPEN
`D-008` · **Owner:** Camden · **Tracked as:** GitHub issue (label `question`, milestone M0)
· **Close this week**

`docs/milestones.md` assumes a semester start of Mon 2026-08-24, placing 2026-09-11 at the
end of Week 3 — meaning **M0 is due next week**. The handout gives weeks, not dates. If the
assumption is off by one week the M4 soak start moves, and M4 already lands on Thanksgiving
week. Verify against the syllabus and mark LOCKED.

---

# G. Superseded

*(none yet — when a decision is replaced, move it here with a pointer to its replacement.
Never delete one. The reasoning is evidence, and "what M2 got wrong" is a graded section of
`docs/DESIGN.md`.)*

---

## Adding a decision

Append it to the right category with the next free `D-###` for citation, and fill every
field. If Claude made it without a human present, it is ⚠️ **UNREVIEWED** and it goes in the
Review Queue at the top — **in the same commit that implements it**, never a later one.

**Closing an open question.** When a human answers a `decision` or `question` issue, the
answer moves here as a 🔒 LOCKED entry citing the issue number, and the issue closes. One
commit does both — resolving one question is one responsibility, however many lines it
touches across this file (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3, documentation rules).

# Problem memo — carwatch (Camden Thomas, Lance Baron)

> **STATUS: M1 DRAFT.** One page maximum. Its job is to survive being read by a
> skeptical stranger. Bracketed items are unfilled.

## The user
> Rubric: a person or place, **named or nameable**. "A cautious driver" is a persona and
> will be returned for revision the same way "people who might want to monitor things"
> would be. Name a human and a car.

[NAME], who drives a [YEAR MAKE MODEL] and [does X with it — commutes N miles, tows,
short-trips it in winter]. And [NAME 2], whose [YEAR MAKE MODEL] does something
measurably different with its miles.

The point of two users is the thesis: the same oil-change sticker says 5,000 miles to
both cars, and the cars disagree.

## The problem
> Observable and costly: what goes wrong, how often, what it costs in money or worry.

Maintenance intervals are generalizations. The sticker on the windshield knows nothing
about how this engine has actually been run — a commuter that never reaches operating
temperature and a highway car with the same odometer reading have not aged the same
way. The consequence runs both directions and both are expensive: oil changed far
earlier than it needed to be, or an engine run on oil that lost its pressure margin
weeks ago. [Fill in a real number: cost of an oil change × frequency, or the cost of
the failure you are trying to catch.]

Meanwhile the car already measures everything needed to know the difference, and
publishes it on a bus, continuously — and then throws it away. The check-engine light
is the only thing that ever reads it, and it is a **threshold on a single value that
fires after the damage.**

## Why a device
> The 3 a.m. test: why must something be physically present and always awake? And why
> doesn't a phone app already solve this?

The signal is a slow trend across weeks of driving, and it is only interpretable if you
have the cold starts, the short trips, and the long pulls — *all* of them, not the
drives someone remembered to open an app for. A phone app is present for the trips you
thought to instrument, which is a biased sample of exactly the variable being measured.

The interesting moment is also never the moment anyone is looking: it is the third cold
start of a February week where warm-up took ninety seconds longer than it did in
January. Nobody is holding a phone then. The device is in the car, awake at key-on,
recording before anyone has decided anything is wrong.

And the data stays in the car. No account, no upload, no fleet telematics company
holding a log of everywhere this person drove.

## The sensors
> Which two (or more) and how they **cooperate** rather than coexist.

The vehicle's own sensors, read as raw CAN frames: oil pressure, coolant temperature,
intake air temperature, MAP, O2 / fuel trims, RPM, engine load.

They cooperate because **no one of them means anything alone.** Oil pressure is a
function of RPM and oil temperature; the diagnostic signal is the *residual* after
normalizing for both, which requires all three sensors to reach one conclusion. Fuel
trim is only interpretable against load. Coolant temperature only indicts a thermostat
once ambient temperature and load have been accounted for. Every verdict this device
produces requires at least two sensors to agree on something a single threshold cannot
see.

[If D-006 resolves to adding physical sensors: an MPU-6050 on the engine mount and a
DS18B20 temperature probe, with the vibration spectrum order-tracked against CAN-derived
crank speed — a measurement the ECU itself cannot make.]

## The mechanisms
> First guess at two menu items, one sentence of justification each. May change by M2.

**B — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison.** At 500 kbit/s the MCP2515's
two receive buffers overflow in milliseconds, so a poll loop either burns a core or
loses frames; the `INT` line lets us service the controller only when it has something.

**D — custom append-only storage with crash consistency.** The power is cut mid-write
every single time the key turns off, so the storage layer never gets a clean shutdown
and must recover a torn tail on every boot.

## The risk
> The single thing most likely to sink this project. Name it now.

**That neither testbed publishes analog oil pressure on the bus.** Many consumer
vehicles expose only a binary low-pressure switch, which would delete our headline
diagnostic and leave us with two. The mitigation is a $0 supported-PID scan on both
cars in Week 4 — before the design document, not after (**D-007**).

Second risk, named honestly: the oil-life trend needs a real oil interval to develop,
and that is calendar time we cannot buy back by working harder in Week 14. Baseline
collection starts at M2 or it does not happen.
----
# Wiring and electrical safety

> **The Pi's GPIO is 3.3 V and has zero over-voltage protection.** Feed a pin 5 V and
> it can die silently — sometimes taking the SoC with it. Swap VCC and GND and the
> board usually does not warn you first; it just stops working.
>
> Rules, non-negotiable: **breadboard anything 5 V-adjacent first. Check every voltage
> with a meter before the Pi is ever plugged in. Wire with the board powered off.**

## MCP2515 module → Pi

| MCP2515 | Pi pin | Pi signal | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| VCC | [TBD] | 3.3 V or 5 V | **Read your module.** Many boards run the TJA1050 transceiver at 5 V and level-shift the MCP2515 side; many cheap clones do not and will drive 5 V onto MISO. Verify before connecting. |
| GND | 6 | GND | Common ground with the vehicle. |
| CS | 24 | GPIO8 / SPI0_CE0 | |
| SO (MISO) | 21 | GPIO9 / SPI0_MISO | **Meter this line for 5 V before connecting.** |
| SI (MOSI) | 19 | GPIO10 / SPI0_MOSI | |
| SCK | 23 | GPIO11 / SPI0_SCLK | |
| INT | [TBD] | GPIO25 (proposed) | Edge-triggered. This line *is* mechanism B. |

**Crystal:** note whether your module has an 8 MHz or 16 MHz crystal — it goes straight
into the bitrate configuration and a wrong value produces a silently dead bus.

```
dtoverlay=mcp2515-can0,oscillator=<8000000|16000000>,interrupt=25
dtoverlay=spi0-hw-cs
```

## OBD2 connector

| OBD2 pin | Signal |
|---|---|
| 6 | CAN_H |
| 14 | CAN_L |
| 16 | +12 V battery (always live) |
| 4, 5 | Chassis / signal ground |

**Pin 16 is live with the key off.** That is what makes the unattended soak possible and
what makes a dead battery possible. Fuse it, and measure the device's key-off draw
before leaving it in a car overnight — record the number in `docs/EVALUATION.md`.

## Bring-up order

1. Meter the module's VCC and MISO with the Pi disconnected.
2. Pi + module on the bench, no car. `ip link show can0`.
3. Two-node bench bus (module + USB-to-CAN adapter) — prove frames move before a car is
   ever involved.
4. Car, engine off, key to accessory. `candump can0`.
5. Car, running.

Do not skip step 3. Debugging a silent bus with a car attached is debugging two
unknowns at once.

# docs/board.toml — the single source of truth for the carwatch GitHub board.
#
# CONTRACT
#   This file describes what SHOULD exist on GitHub. `tools/board_sync.py` makes
#   GitHub match it. The sync is a reconciler, not a generator:
#
#     * running it twice changes nothing the second time
#     * items absent from this file are left completely alone (never closed,
#       never edited, never removed from the board) — they are reported as
#       unmanaged and ignored
#     * adding one task means adding one [[item]] block and re-running sync
#     * `slug` is the permanent identity of an item. Issue numbers live in
#       docs/board.lock.json and are derived, never typed here.
#
#   Inside an issue body the sync owns ONLY the region between the
#   <!-- board-sync:deps --> markers. Everything else in a body on GitHub is
#   overwritten from this file, so edit prose HERE, not in the web UI.
#
# EDITING
#   status = backlog | blocked | ready | in-progress | in-review | done
#     Omit it and sync picks the column for you: "backlog" while any blocker is
#     still open, "ready" once nothing blocks it, "done" once the issue closes.
#     Set it explicitly to drive the column by hand — "blocked" is reserved for
#     waiting on something that is not another item (a shipment, a reply).
#   done      closes the issue. Items labeled question/decision additionally
#             require --close-questions, because CLAUDE.md forbids Claude from
#             closing those on its own judgement.
#   blocked_by takes slugs, never issue numbers.
#   decision  optional "D-###". Must exist in docs/DECISIONS.md; sync renders a
#             link line into the managed region and warns about unknown IDs.
#
# Run:  python tools/board_sync.py --check     (report drift, change nothing)
#       python tools/board_sync.py             (reconcile)

[board]
# Identified by NUMBER, not title: matching on a name is how you end up writing to
# one project while reading another in the browser. This is the project linked to
# the repository — the one the repo's Projects tab opens.
number = 1
title = "carwatch"
columns = ["Backlog", "Ready", "In progress", "In review", "Done"]
# Sync maps board.toml statuses onto whatever Status options the project has
# (COLUMN_PREFERENCE in board_sync.py) rather than rewriting the field, because
# rewriting it discards every card's current value. `blocked` therefore lands in
# Backlog here, which is what we want anyway. Set reshape_status = true only to
# deliberately rebuild the Status field from `columns`.
# reshape_status = false

[people]
camden = "CamdenThomas"
lance = "Lance-Baron"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ labels

[[label]]
name = "question"
color = "d876e3"
description = "Needs a human answer. Claude may never close this."

[[label]]
....
milestone = "M0"
labels = ["question"]
owner = "camden"
decision = "D-008"
title = "M0 question: verify M0-M6 dates against the syllabus"
body = '''

It's Camden's session. I've read CLAUDE.md, milestones, DECISIONS, the problem memo, the wiring doc, the BOM and the live issue list. I haven't made any edits or created a branch yet. This is a new hardware decision that touches Lance's car and Lance's schematic, so §7.8 says I need your yes first.

## 1. The splice-behind-the-port design

Taking power from the OBD2 plug (pin 16) and splicing CAN-H/CAN-L behind the port keeps D-001 (MCP2515 on SPI) intact and doesn't reopen any LOCKED decision. Four things need settling before it goes into DECISIONS as D-011.

**What is your reason for splicing?** The wires behind the port are the same wires as pins 6 and 14, so a splice there carries exactly the same traffic the port does.
- **If the goal is getting past a security gateway** (newer cars often only pass diagnostic request/response traffic at the port), a splice right behind the port won't help. You'd have to tap the bus on the car's side of the gateway module, which is a much bigger job. Your ELM327 can answer this for about $12: run `ATMA` (monitor all) at the port. If you see a steady flood of broadcast frames, there's no gateway problem and the splice isn't needed for data. If the port is quiet except when you ask it something, a gateway is in the way.
- **If the goal is keeping the port free** (for scan tools and emissions inspection) and **having a solid connection that lasts the semester**, those are good reasons. A pass-through OBD Y-splitter gives you the same wiring with no cutting. On Lance's daily driver, I'd strongly suggest that version, or a T-tap that doesn't cut anything, over cutting the harness. Lance has to agree to it either way.

**Rules for the device being a permanent stub on the engine's CAN bus:**
- **Remove the 120 Ω termination jumper on the MCP2515 module.** The car already has its own termination, and adding ours drops the bus to about 40 Ω.
- **Keep the tap wires short.** At 500 kbit/s, aim for under about 0.3 m.
- **Use listen-only mode by default.** Otherwise a bug in our code could send error frames onto the engine's bus of a car someone drives every day.

**Listen-only conflicts with D-005.** D-005's plan is to start with standard Mode 01 PIDs, and those only arrive if we transmit requests. That leaves two options:
- **Stay passive:** use only the car's broadcast frames. This means decoding manufacturer-specific frames on each car, which is more work.
- **Send occasional requests:** a low-rate, rate-limited requester, and we accept that the device transmits on the bus.

This needs a human decision. I'd lean toward the requester but keep a listen-only build flag.

**Knowing when the key turns off gets easier.** The bus goes quiet at key-off while pin 16 stays live. That quiet period is a natural trigger to flush storage (mechanism D) and to cut the device's current draw.

## 2. The M1 deadline (Sun 2026-09-27, 6 days out)

Two caveats: D-008 means the dates are still unverified, and M0 was due yesterday with 6 issues still open. The one that matters is **#4, order hardware**. Every M1 critical-path item waits on the ELM327.

| Day | Camden | Lance |

| **Sat** | Copy transcripts (#17). Clean up M0 leftovers: the soak email (#7) and dates (#6). | Copy transcripts (#17). Sign the decision log (#10). |
| **Sun** | Open the PR. A human merges it. | — |

**Schedule risk:** #15 (the memo) is currently blocked on #13, which is blocked on both surveys. If the ELM327 hasn't arrived by Thursday, the memo misses the deadline. I recommend removing #13 from the memo's `blocked_by`. The memo can name the risk honestly while the survey is still pending, and the answer gets filled in when it lands. A free scan at an auto-parts store is a fallback for the supported-PID bitmaps, but not for the `ATMA` gateway check.

content.text: okay and if we ignore the obd2 port all together can we relaiably just tap into CAN on a non modulated line? lets just think about lances honda crv, can we power it and tap CAN non invasivly practically for this assignment?

Yes. For a CR-V there are practical ways to tap CAN and get power without cutting anything. Which one works depends on the model year, which is still open issue #5. One wording point first: CAN isn't modulated, it's a plain differential signal. I'll read "non-modulated line" as "a line that isn't filtered by a gateway module", meaning you'd see the car's raw broadcast traffic.

## Tapping CAN without the OBD2 port

**1. Pass-through harness at the forward camera (best option, if the car has Honda Sensing).** CR-Vs with Honda Sensing have a lane-keep camera behind the rearview mirror, and its connector carries the main powertrain CAN bus (F-CAN). Honda Sensing was standard on upper trims from 2017 and on all trims from about 2020. The openpilot community taps Hondas at exactly this point. They use a pass-through harness: unplug the camera, plug the harness in between, plug the camera back in. That gives you:
- no cutting, fully reversible in two minutes
- the tap sits on the car's side of any gateway, so you see the real broadcast traffic
- often switched 12 V on the same connector

The catch is that you're splicing into a safety system's wiring. A bad connection could disable lane-keep or collision braking. The device must be listen-only and must never break the camera's own connection.

**2. Contactless CAN reader.** These are inductive or capacitive clamps from fleet telematics, sold as "contactless CAN reader" or "CAN crocodile", at roughly $50–100. They clip over a twisted pair and read through the insulation, then output their own CAN signal that the MCP2515 can read. They can't transmit, so they're safe by design. Downsides:
- you need a wiring diagram to find the right pair
- we'd be trusting a black box between the bus and our code
- they rule out Mode 01 requests

**3. Insulation-piercing T-taps** (for example Posi-Tap) on the twisted pair. Low effort, but they pierce the wire, so this isn't truly non-invasive on Lance's car. I'd rank it last.

## Power without the OBD2 port

- **Add-a-fuse tap in the interior fuse box (recommended).** It's reversible, fused, and standard practice. Put it on an ignition-switched circuit and you get three things at once:
  - key-on/key-off detection for free
  - no battery drain while parked
  - the real power cut on every key-off that mechanism D is designed around
- **The 12 V accessory socket.** Zero tools, but the plug can get knocked loose, and you need to check whether the socket turns off with the key.

Either way it goes through the automotive buck converter already on the BOM.

## Two things that could make this unnecessary, or not worth it

1. **The OBD2 port may already show the raw bus.** If Lance runs the $12 ELM327 `ATMA` check on the port and sees constant broadcast traffic, a Y-splitter at the port is the least risky option, and options 1–3 add risk for nothing. Do this test before buying any harness.
2. **What data does the tap actually give us?** Broadcast frames use Honda's own formats, not the standard Mode 01 PIDs. Community decode files exist (opendbc), which would save weeks. But before we lean on them, we should ask Pallickara whether third-party decode tables are allowed. They aren't model weights, so D-004 probably doesn't forbid them, but the question belongs in the same email as the soak question (#7). Separately, I believe many Hondas have only an on/off oil-pressure switch, not a pressure sensor. If so, diagnostic #1 (oil pressure) has a problem no matter where we tap (#13).

## What would settle it

Lance can answer most of this in about 15 minutes at the car:
1. Year and trim, and whether it has Honda Sensing (closes #5).
2. A photo of the camera connector behind the mirror.
3. The fuse-box diagram from the manual or the lid, showing which circuits turn off with the key.
4. The `ATMA` capture at the OBD2 port, 60 seconds with the engine running.

Once we have those, I'll write the tap choice up as D-011 (UNREVIEWED, needing Lance's sign-off) and put the matching items on the board. Until then I'm not committing to any option. §8.4 applies: I can't see the car, and the capture is the evidence.
2015 honda crv exl

That settles the most important question: **a 2015 CR-V EX-L doesn't have Honda Sensing.** In 2015, lane-keep and collision braking came only on the Touring trim, so there's no lane-keep camera connector to tap. The EX-L's LaneWatch camera is a video feed, not CAN. That rules out the camera-harness option.

## What this means for the Honda

**The OBD2 port is back to being the best tap point.** It's a 2015 model, well before security gateways were common on consumer cars, so I don't expect anything filtering the port. Mode 01 PIDs at the port are a legal emissions requirement and will work regardless. What's still unverified is whether the port also shows **broadcast** traffic, or only replies to requests. The `ATMA` check answers that. Either result works for us:

| `ATMA` result | Meaning | Tap |
|---|---|---|
| Constant traffic at the port | The main CAN bus is wired straight to the port | Y-splitter at the port; we can use broadcast frames plus Mode 01 |
| Quiet unless we ask | The port only answers requests | Still a Y-splitter; we poll Mode 01 at a limited rate |

A contactless clamp or T-tap would only be worth the trouble if we specifically needed broadcast frames and the port turned out to be quiet. I'd leave those options aside unless the capture forces us back to them.

**Power:** a Y-splitter gives us pin 16. If we want switched power so the device can't drain Lance's battery, use an add-a-fuse tap on a circuit that turns off with the key. Both are reversible.

## Two things this changes elsewhere

1. **Oil pressure (the named risk, #13).** I believe the 2015 refresh's 2.4 L engine (K24W) has only an on/off oil-pressure *switch*, not a pressure sensor. If so, diagnostic #1 can't work on the Honda from any tap point. The Outback survey (#11) may still save it on one car. I'm reasoning from general Honda practice, not a service manual, so the PID survey confirms it: check whether oil pressure appears in the supported list.

2. **The problem memo's thesis.** A 2015 CR-V doesn't go by a windshield sticker. It has Honda's **Maintenance Minder**, which estimates oil life from how the engine has been run. A skeptical reader will ask "doesn't the car already do this?" The honest answer is that the Minder is an *estimate from a usage model*; it never measures the engine's actual condition, and our device measures. PROBLEM.md needs to make that argument directly instead of "the sticker is generic."

3. **Mechanism B's justification weakens if the port is quiet.** Our argument for interrupts is that a busy 500 kbit/s bus overflows the MCP2515's buffers in milliseconds. If the Honda's port only answers requests, the Outback's capture has to carry that argument.

## Recording it

The Honda answer closes #5. Closing it is a human's job (and it's Lance's issue), but I can put the answer into the files, and #12, the Honda PID survey, becomes workable once the ELM327 arrives. On a branch, that's one commit: fill in the Honda answer under DECISIONS A.3 (D-007) as UNREVIEWED for Lance, and add the port-traffic check to the #12 body in `board.toml`. I can't run the board sync until Python is reinstalled on this machine.

Want me to go ahead with that commit, or wait until Lance has run the `ATMA` capture so the tap decision (D-011) goes in with evidence?

now under the frame work that you can plug it into the obd2 port and then into a usbc power supy from the car (or cigrette lighter) and the pi is what plugs in records data i think that could be marketable to everyone, then you connect your phone to view the status, it could even have a warning light. we are building the model to prove its worth not the end all million doller product

That framing works, and it fits our rules better than the splice did. The phone isn't a loophole in the no-network rule: §2.1 allows serving the device's own local network, so the Pi runs its own Wi-Fi hotspot and serves a status page, with no cloud and no app store. Here's how it lands on everything we've already decided.

## What the framing strengthens

- **It answers the phone-app test.** Plug-in dongles with phone apps already exist, and they only record while the phone is connected and the app is open. In our design the Pi is the part that's always awake and recording; the phone is just a window onto it. That's the "why a device" argument in one sentence.
- **Plug-and-play pushes us toward standard Mode 01 PIDs**, which settles the listen-only question from earlier. Mode 01 PIDs work on every car since 1996, while broadcast decoding is different for each make. A device that "learns *this* car's normal" from the universal PIDs is what makes it work on any car without per-model decode work. Proposed: rate-limited Mode 01 requests are the main path, and broadcast frames are an extra where a car has them.
- **The warning light is worth it.** It's one GPIO pin and an LED. It makes "honest reporting through our own interface" (demo-day movement 1) visible from across the room, and it answers the 3 a.m. test: nobody is looking at a phone then. It has to follow the same hysteresis as every other verdict (D.3). A light that flickers gets ignored.

## What USB-C car power changes (measure it, don't assume)

- **Current.** A Pi 4 wants 5.1 V at 3 A; a Pi 5 wants 5 A. Many built-in car USB ports supply 1–2.4 A, and voltage sags when the engine cranks. Plan on a quality 12 V-socket USB-C adapter rated at least 3 A. Then prove it with `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start. That output is our evidence, and it goes into EVALUATION.
- **Car USB and 12 V sockets usually turn off with the key.** That's good: no battery drain, and mechanism D's defining constraint ("power is cut mid-write at every key-off") becomes literally true. It also rules out option (c) for the soak question D-006 (a parked-car soak on live CAN), so the fallback is (b), extra physical sensors, or the professor's answer.
- **Ground.** The CAN transceiver still needs OBD pin 5 as its signal ground even though power comes from elsewhere. That's one wire in the Y-harness.
- **BOM.** The 12 V→5 V buck converter probably drops out, replaced by the USB-C adapter.

## One thing to keep narrow

"Marketable to everyone" belongs in PROBLEM.md as *why it matters*, not as the user or the claim. The rubric returns personas, and "everyone" is the biggest persona there is. The memo still names you with the Outback and Lance with the 2015 CR-V. The claim we defend stays E.1: three faults, two cars, measured error rates. Your last sentence is exactly the right attitude, and it's worth putting nearly word for word in the memo: *this is a prototype built to prove the idea is worth something, not the finished product.*

## What I'd write, on your go-ahead

Branch `camden/m1/product-topology`, with two commits:

2. **`M1 docs`: PROBLEM.md draft.** Named users, the Maintenance Minder counter-argument, why-a-device written around the Pi-plus-phone split, and the oil-pressure risk. This makes progress on #15 but doesn't close it: the risk section waits on the PID surveys.

=================== docs/DESIGN.md
     1	# Design document — carwatch
     2	
     3	> **STATUS: M2 SKELETON.** 3–5 pages when complete. The handout calls these "the most
     4	> leveraged hours of the whole project" — every hour of arguing here saves five of
     5	> rewriting later.
     6	>
     7	> **Before submitting, run the three-isolated-workers check:** a design-only reviewer,
     8	> a parts-only buyer who never sees the design, and a builder who only follows
     9	> instructions must each succeed from their own section alone.
    10	
    11	## 1. Architecture
    12	> A diagram in the spirit of the handout's Figure 1: processes, threads, kernel
    13	> components, data flows, **and rates on every arrow**. The rates are not decoration —
    14	> they are what makes the mechanism justifications checkable.
    15	
    16	```
    17	  OBD2 connector
    18	  pin 6 / pin 14
    19	        │ CAN 500 kbit/s
    20	        ▼
    21	  ┌──────────────┐  SPI0 @ [N] MHz     ┌────────────────┐
    22	  │ MCP2515 +    │────────────────────▶│   candaemon    │  [mech B]
    23	  │ TJA1050      │  INT ──▶ GPIO[N]    │  IRQ RX path   │
    24	  └──────────────┘  edge-triggered     └───────┬────────┘
    25	                                               │ SPSC ring, [N] frames/s  [mech F]
    26	                                               │ shm, sequence-accounted
    27	                    ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
    28	                    ▼                          ▼                      ▼
    29	            ┌───────────────┐         ┌────────────────┐     ┌────────────────┐
    30	            │   storaged    │         │   analyzed     │     │   obdctl       │
    31	            │ append-only   │◀────────│ features →     │────▶│ query CLI      │
    32	            │ CRC, fsync    │  read   │ baseline →     │ UDS │ 5 verbs        │
    33	            │   [mech D]    │         │ model → FSM    │     └────────────────┘
    34	            └───────────────┘         └────────────────┘
    35	                    ▲                          ▲
    36	                    └──────────┬───────────────┘
    37	                               │ spawn / heartbeat / restart-with-backoff
    38	                        ┌──────────────┐
    39	                        │  supervisor  │  [mech E]
    40	                        └──────────────┘
    41	```
    42	
    43	**TODO(M2):** fill every `[N]`. Replace with a real figure in `docs/figures/`.
    44	
    45	## 2. Mechanism mapping
    46	> For each chosen menu item: which component implements it, and a justification **from
    47	> the user's requirements**. The defense will test the justification, not the choice.
    48	> Model the form on the handout's example: "the vibration analysis is meaningless above
    49	> 2 ms of sampling jitter, hence SCHED_FIFO."
    50	
    51	See `docs/decisions/D-002-mechanism-commitments.md` for the committed rationale; expand
    52	each here with the measured numbers that justify it.
    53	
    54	| Menu item | Component | Justification from requirements | How measured |
    55	|---|---|---|---|
    56	| B | `src/can/` | | event-latency distribution + CPU, IRQ vs poll, idle and loaded |
    57	| D | `src/store/` | | recovery after mid-write power cut, N trials |
    58	| E | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` | | `kill -9` any child; detection/degradation/recovery in the log |
    59	| F | `src/ipc/ring.c` | | sustained rate, zero drops, sequence-accounted, under contention |
    60	
    61	## 3. Failure-mode table
    62	> For each component: how it can fail, how the failure is **detected**, what the system
    63	> **does**, and what the **log will show**. The soak test grades this table's honesty —
    64	> so write the modes you are afraid of, not the ones you have already handled.
    65	
    66	| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log line |
    67	|---|---|---|---|---|
    68	| MCP2515 | physically unplugged mid-drive | | degrade, do not restart-storm | |
    69	| MCP2515 | SPI transaction timeout | | | |
    70	| candaemon | crash / `kill -9` | supervisor `waitpid` | restart with backoff | |
    71	| ring | consumer stalls, producer would overwrite | sequence gap accounting | | |
    72	| storaged | disk full | | | |
    73	| storaged | power cut mid-write | CRC mismatch on recovery scan | truncate torn tail | |
    74	| analyzed | model file missing or corrupt | | fall back to residuals only | |
    75	| supervisor | itself dies | systemd `Restart=always` | | |
    76	| clock | no RTC, time jumps at boot | | | |
    77	
    78	## 4. Storage and data
    79	> What is stored, at what rate, in what format, with what retention, and what happens to
    80	> it when the power dies mid-write.
    81	
    82	- **Record format:** [magic][seq][mono_ns][wall_ns][src: live|replay|synth][pid][value][crc32]
    83	- **Rates:** [fill]
    84	- **Retention and rollup:** [fill — raw window, then binned aggregates?]
    85	- **fsync discipline:** [fill — batch size, interval, and the argument for it]
    86	- **Crash story:** [fill — recovery scan, torn-tail truncation, what is lost and why
    87	  losing it is acceptable]
    88	- **Baseline persistence:** learned per-bin statistics must survive a power cut. This is
    89	  the requirement that made mechanism D non-optional.
    90	
    91	## 5. Constraints and substitutions
    92	> What the ideal build would use, what we are actually using, and what the gap costs.
    93	> "A design document with nothing to report here has usually not met its hardware yet."
    94	
    95	| Wanted | Using | What the substitution costs |
    96	|---|---|---|
    97	| Analog oil pressure sender, direct | Whatever the ECU publishes (D-007) | Possibly binary switch only — headline diagnostic at risk |
    98	| A year of failing engines | Induced faults on two healthy cars | Only three fault classes, and none of them is a real bearing failure |
    99	| 48h of live driving | [pending D-006] | |
   100	
   101	## 6. Evaluation plan
   102	> The measurements we will take, each with **method and committed target**. Numbers
   103	> committed now are twice as credible when hit later, and instructive either way.
   104	
   105	| Measurement | Method | Target |
   106	|---|---|---|
   107	| CAN frame → stored, p50/p99 | timestamp at IRQ and at fsync | |
   108	| IRQ vs polling: latency + CPU | both paths, idle and `stress-ng` loaded | |
   109	| Drop rate under contention | sequence accounting | zero |
   110	| RSS per process over 48h | hourly heartbeat, plotted | flat |
   111	| Detection: TPR / FPR per diagnostic | induced-fault fixtures | |
   112	| Recovery after mid-write power cut | N pull-the-plug trials | 100% |
   113	
   114	## 7. Ownership map
   115	| Owner | Subsystems |
   116	|---|---|
   117	| Camden | `src/can/`, `src/capture/`, `src/ipc/`, `drivers/` |
   118	| Lance | `src/store/`, `src/analysis/`, `tools/train/` |
   119	| Shared | `src/supervisor/`, `src/interface/`, `src/common/`, docs |
   120	
   121	Ownership means first authorship and answerability at the defense, not exclusivity.
   122	
   123	## 8. AI-use plan
   124	> What we use Claude Code for, what we don't, and how the §3.3 boundary stays visible
   125	> in the repository.
   126	
   127	Used for: planning, explaining kernel and SPI mechanics, drafting test fixtures,
   128	adversarial review of diffs, documentation. Not used for: the analysis pipeline's
   129	design decisions, and never at runtime.
   130	
   131	The boundary is legible by inspection: `src/` contains no HTTP client and no network
   132	code except the LAN interface in `src/interface/`. `grep -r` for any network symbol
   133	outside that directory returns nothing, and that check is in `make test`.
   134	
   135	## 9. Changelog (added at M5)
   136	> What M2's version got wrong. This section is graded and an empty one is not credible.
=================== docs/PLAN.md
     1	# carwatch — full project plan
     2	
     3	**This file is the *why*. `docs/board.toml` is the *what*.**
     4	
     5	The work breakdown that used to live here — 80 numbered tasks with owners and blocked-by
     6	lists — moved to `docs/board.toml`, which `tools/board_sync.py` reconciles onto GitHub
     7	issues and the `carwatch` project board. Keeping a second copy here would guarantee the two
     8	disagreed by Week 9, and nothing would have told us which one was wrong.
     9	
    10	So: read **this** for why the plan is shaped this way and what to sacrifice when it slips.
    11	Read **the board** for what to do next. See `docs/BOARD.md` for how the board works.
    12	
    13	- Decisions already made: `docs/DECISIONS.md`
    14	- Milestone exit criteria: `docs/milestones.md`
    15	- The rubric itself: `docs/handout/CS370-TermProject.md`
    16	
    17	Items are named below by their board **slug**, which is permanent. Issue numbers are not
    18	written into any document — they live only in `docs/board.lock.json`, which sync maintains.
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	## 1. The two critical paths
    23	
    24	Everything else has slack. These two do not, and they are the only reasons this project
    25	fails in Week 14.
    26	
    27	### Critical path A — calendar, not effort: the oil interval
    28	
    29	Diagnostic #1 claims oil pressure degrades measurably across an oil-change interval. **That
    30	claim needs a real interval to develop, and an interval is calendar time you cannot buy
    31	back by working harder.**
    32	
    33	```
    34	baseline collection starts ──── 5-7 weeks of driving ────▶ oil change ──── 2 weeks ────▶ trend is real
    35	        M2 (mid-Oct)                                       (~mid-Nov)                     M4 (late Nov)
    36	```
    37	
    38	**Consequence:** logging must be running on both cars by the end of M2, even if the code
    39	is ugly, even if it is just `candump` to a file. A crude capture that starts on time beats
    40	an elegant one that starts three weeks late. **If baseline collection has not started by the
    41	M2 deadline, diagnostic #1 is dead** and we fall back to diagnostics #2 and #3 — decide that
    42	consciously, record it in `DECISIONS.md`, and narrow the claim in writing.
    43	
    44	Board chain: `order` → `bench` → `twonode` → `firstcap` → **`baseline`** → `foil`.
    45	
    46	### Critical path B — hardware lead time
    47	
    48	```
    49	order (M0) ──▶ arrives ──▶ bench bring-up ──▶ two-node bench bus ──▶ first live car capture ──▶ pipeline (M3)
    50	```
    51	
    52	Nothing downstream of "arrives" can start early. The handout names shipping time as the most
    53	common silent schedule-killer, twice. **Order on the day you read this**, and order the $12
    54	ELM327 in the same cart — it unblocks the PID survey weeks before the MCP2515 matters.
    55	
    56	Board chain: `order` blocks `pidsub`, `pidhonda`, `bench` and `meterv` — five of the eight
    57	M0/M1 items and everything physical after them.
    58	
    59	### The one cheap experiment that de-risks everything
    60	
    61	**The PID survey (`pidsub` on the Outback, `pidhonda` on the Honda).** Ten minutes per car,
    62	$12, no custom hardware. It answers the project's named risk: *does either testbed actually
    63	publish analog oil pressure?* If the answer is no, we find out in Week 4 with the whole
    64	design still soft, instead of Week 11 with the analysis engine half-written around a value
    65	that does not exist. Both feed `oilq`, which is where the answer gets recorded.
    66	
    67	---
    68	
    69	## 2. Phase structure
    70	
    71	| Phase | Weeks | Theme | The thing that must be true at the end |
    72	|---|---|---|---|
    73	| **M0** | 4 | Commit and order | Parts ordered, questions asked, board live |
    74	| **M1** | 5 | Know the problem | A named user, a named risk, and PID survey results |
    75	| **M2** | 6–7 | Argue on paper | Design settled, **logging running on both cars** |
    76	| **M3** | 8–10 | Build the spine | Frames → ring → disk, supervised, on a real car |
    77	| **M4** | 11–14 | Make it smart, then prove it | Analysis done, experiments measured, soak passed |
    78	| **M5** | 15 | Account for it honestly | Report written, limits named, history clean |
    79	| **M6** | 15–16 | Defend it | Both partners fluent in both halves |
    80	
    81	---
    82	
    83	## 3. What to cut, and in what order
    84	
    85	The device shipped in Week 15 will be smaller than the one planned in Week 4. Decide the
    86	order now, while it is cheap, so the decision is not made at 2 a.m. in Week 13:
    87	
    88	1. **The second vehicle** — `pidhonda`, and the Honda half of `fvac` / `fcool` / `foil`.
    89	   Halves the decode and baseline work. Costs the strongest five seconds of the demo, but
    90	   not the grade.
    91	2. **Diagnostic #1 (oil)** if critical path A slips — `foil`, and the oil claim in
    92	   `docs/PROBLEM.md`. Fall back to #2 and #3, narrow the claim in writing, and say so in the
    93	   limitations section.
    94	3. **The trained classifier** — `train`, `infer`. The features are the intelligence;
    95	   residuals and trends still produce verdicts without it. Say so at the defense.
    96	4. **The remaining `obdctl` verbs** — `obdrest`, down to `status` + `verdicts`.
    97	
    98	**Never cut, in any circumstance:** the soak (`soak1`), the mechanism comparison
    99	experiments (`expirq`, `expdrop`, `expcrash`), the limitations section (`evalreport`), or
   100	the transcript copy-outs (`tx1`–`tx4`). Those are graded directly, and three of them cannot
   101	be reconstructed after the fact.
   102	
   103	**How to cut, mechanically.** Do not delete the `[[item]]` — a deleted item leaves an open
   104	issue behind that sync no longer manages, and the decision to cut disappears with it.
   105	Instead: record the cut in `DECISIONS.md`, add a line to the item's body saying it was cut
   106	and why, set `status = "done"`, and close the issue by hand. The board then shows a cut that
   107	was made deliberately rather than a task that quietly stopped being mentioned.
   108	
   109	---
   110	
   111	## 4. Standing weekly rhythm
   112	
   113	- **Monday:** `python tools/board_sync.py --check`, then work the **Ready** column. Cards
   114	  move out of Backlog on their own as blockers close — what you are looking for is anything
   115	  Ready that nobody has picked up, and anything still Backlog that should not be.
   116	- **Both partners, every session:** read the `DECISIONS.md` review queue and sign or contest.
   117	- **Friday:** cross-review at least one of the other's merged PRs, and log it in
   118	  `PROMPTLOG.md` while it is fresh.
   119	- **Every milestone:** transcripts out, no exceptions, before anything else is submitted.
   120	- **End of every session:** `python tools/board_sync.py`. A run with nothing to do writes
   121	  nothing, so there is no excuse for skipping it.
=================== README.md
     1	# carwatch
     2	
     3	An always-on in-vehicle diagnostic recorder. It reads a car's own sensors off the CAN
     4	bus, learns what *that specific car* looks like at each operating point, and reports
     5	developing faults that a mileage sticker and a check-engine light both miss.
     6	
     7	CS 370 Operating Systems term project — Camden Thomas & Lance Baron, Colorado State
     8	University.
     9	
    10	> **Status: M0 scaffolding.** Structure and contracts are in place; subsystems are
    11	> stubs. See `docs/milestones.md`.
    12	
    13	## What it does
    14	
    15	| Diagnostic | Sensors that cooperate | Why a threshold can't do it |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| Oil pressure degradation across oil life | oil pressure + RPM + coolant temp | Oil pressure is a function of RPM and oil temperature. The signal is the *residual* after normalizing for both, trended over weeks. |
    18	| Cooling system anomaly | coolant temp + ambient/intake temp + engine load | A short-cycling thermostat has a period and amplitude. A single temperature reading has neither. |
    19	| Mixture drift (vacuum leak / failing O2 / dirty MAF) | short+long term fuel trim + MAP + RPM | Trim values are only meaningful relative to load; the diagnosis is which way trims move *as load changes*. |
    20	
    21	## Hardware
    22	
    23	See `docs/hardware/BOM.md` for the parts list and `docs/hardware/wiring.md` for the
    24	pinout and the 3.3 V safety notes. Summary: Raspberry Pi 4, MCP2515 + TJA1050 CAN
    25	module on SPI0 with `INT` on a GPIO, OBD2 pigtail (CAN_H pin 6, CAN_L pin 14).
    26	
    27	## Quick start (clean Raspberry Pi OS)
    28

    30	git clone <repo> && cd CS370-Term-Project

     1	# carwatch
     2	
     3	An always-on in-vehicle diagnostic recorder. It reads a car's own sensors off the CAN
     4	bus, learns what *that specific car* looks like at each operating point, and reports
     5	developing faults that a mileage sticker and a check-engine light both miss.
     6	
     7	CS 370 Operating Systems term project — Camden Thomas & Lance Baron, Colorado State
     8	University.

    11	> stubs. See `docs/milestones.md`.

    13	## What it does
    14	
    15	| Diagnostic | Sensors that cooperate | Why a threshold can't do it |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| Oil pressure degradation across oil life | oil pressure + RPM + coolant temp | Oil pressure is a function of RPM and oil temperature. The signal is the *residual* after normalizing for both, trended over weeks. |
    18	| Cooling system anomaly | coolant temp + ambient/intake temp + engine load | A short-cycling thermostat has a period and amplitude. A single temperature reading has neither. |
    19	| Mixture drift (vacuum leak / failing O2 / dirty MAF) | short+long term fuel trim + MAP + RPM | Trim values are only meaningful relative to load; the diagnosis is which way trims move *as load changes*. |

     5	> measurements — which is why the defense draws so heavily on this document. Every
     6	> number in here must be one you can reproduce while someone watches.

    10	how many trials. Enough for a TA to re-measure.

    18	- Histogram, not a table of means. [figure]

    22	> heartbeats give you this series for free — plot it.

    27	to die has not passed the soak; it has outrun it.

    38	> system did, and **the log excerpt proving it**.

    52	needed to match the interrupt design's drop rate — that comparison is the point.

=================== docs/hardware/pid-survey.md
     1	# Supported-PID survey
     2	
     3	**Blocks D-007 and the whole of diagnostic #1. Run this before M2.**
     4	
     5	Method: query Mode 01 PIDs `0x00`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x60` — each returns a 32-bit
     6	bitmap of which PIDs in the next block the ECU supports. A $12 ELM327 does this in ten
     7	minutes per car; no need to wait on the MCP2515 hardware.
     8	
     9	## What we specifically need to know
    10	
    11	| PID | Signal | Outback | Honda | Notes |
    12	|---|---|---|---|---|
    13	| 0x0C | RPM | | | |
    14	| 0x04 | Calculated load | | | |
    15	| 0x05 | Coolant temp | | | |
    16	| 0x0F | Intake air temp | | | |
    17	| 0x0B | MAP | | | |
    18	| 0x06/0x07 | Short/long term fuel trim B1 | | | |
    19	| 0x5C | Engine oil temp | | | |
    20	| **—** | **Oil pressure** | | | **Usually NOT a standard PID.** Check for a manufacturer-specific frame, or accept that only a binary low-pressure switch exists. |
    21	| 0x2F | Fuel level | | | |
    22	| 0x31 | Distance since codes cleared | | | odometer proxy for oil-age trending |
    23	
    24	## If oil pressure is unavailable on both vehicles
    25	
    26	Options, in order of preference:
    27	1. Sniff manufacturer-specific frames for an analog pressure value (real work, real
    28	   payoff, and exactly the CAN reverse-engineering this project was originally about).
    29	2. Add a physical pressure sender with a T-fitting at the sender port. Real automotive
    30	   work on a daily driver — do not commit to this after Week 10.
    31	3. Replace diagnostic #1 with an oil-*temperature*-based thermal-load metric and say so
    32	   plainly in docs/DESIGN.md §5 as a declared substitution.
    33	
    34	Record the outcome here and update `docs/decisions/D-003-narrow-the-claim.md`.
=================== docs/hardware/schematic-conventions.md
     1	# Schematic conventions
     2	
     3	**Owner: Lance.** The KiCad project lives in `electricalDrawing/`.
     4	`make hwcheck` must pass before any PR touching it is opened.
     5	
     6	## Scope: schematic yes, PCB probably no
     7	
     8	**Decision A.4 in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.** We capture the schematic; we do not fabricate a
     9	board unless we take The Reach (handout §14).
    10	
    11	A custom PCB earns **zero points** — the rubric grades mechanisms, measurements and the
    12	soak — and adds fab turnaround on top of critical path B, which is already the thing most
    13	likely to delay M2. A breadboard plus an off-the-shelf MCP2515 module clears every
    14	guardrail, and the handout is explicit that the enclosure can be a food container.
    15	
    16	The schematic is worth the time anyway, because three graded artifacts depend on it:
    17	
    18	- `docs/DESIGN.md` needs an architecture diagram and a defensible wiring story
    19	- `docs/hardware/wiring.md` needs pin assignments that cannot drift from reality
    20	- The **three-isolated-workers test** needs a parts-only buyer who can order from the BOM
    21	  without ever seeing the design
    22	
    23	`electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.kicad_pcb` stays in the repo, empty, on purpose — the
    24	same way `src/capture/` does. Its emptiness is a recorded position, not an oversight.
    25	
    26	## Sheet structure
    27	
    28	Lance has blocked out functional areas on the root sheet. Keep that shape; it maps onto the
    29	architecture, which makes both documents easier to defend:
    30	
    31	| Block | Contains |
    32	|---|---|
    33	| **Power** | OBD2 pin 16 (+12 V, **live with the key off**), fuse, 12 V→5 V buck, bulk and bypass caps, the Pi's 5 V rail |
    34	| **CAN** | OBD2 pin 6 / pin 14, TJA1050 transceiver, MCP2515, crystal + load caps, termination decision, `INT` to GPIO |
    35	| **Pi interface** | 40-pin header, SPI0 (CE0/MISO/MOSI/SCLK), the interrupt GPIO, grounds |
    36	| **Sensors** *(conditional, D-006)* | MPU-6050 on I2C with pull-ups; DS18B20 on 1-Wire with its 4.7 kΩ |
    37	
    38	## Rules
    39	
    40	1. **Every net that leaves a block is a named label**, not a wire crossing a boundary. The
    41	   netlist is read by humans at the defense.
    42	2. **Annotate the voltage domain on every power net** (`+12V_SW`, `+5V`, `+3V3`). The Pi has
    43	   no 5 V-tolerant inputs and no over-voltage protection; a mislabeled rail is how a Pi dies
    44	   silently in Week 13.
    45	3. **Every IC gets its decoupling drawn**, even when the module already has it. The
    46	   schematic documents what is *electrically true*, not what we happened to buy assembled.
    47	4. **The MCP2515 crystal frequency is a value field, not a comment** — 8 MHz vs 16 MHz
    48	   changes the device-tree overlay, and a wrong value produces a silently dead bus.
    49	5. **No `DNP`/`no-connect` without a reason in the field.** Floating inputs are an ERC
    50	   violation for good reasons.
    51	6. **`make hwcheck` green before the PR.** ERC violations are build failures, exactly like
    52	   `-Werror`.
    53	
    54	## What must not be trusted to a datasheet alone
    55	
    56	The cheap MCP2515 breakout modules vary: some run the TJA1050 at 5 V and level-shift the
    57	controller side, and some do not — those drive **5 V onto MISO** and will kill a Pi.
    58	
    59	**Meter it. With the Pi disconnected. Before anything is plugged in.** This is the exact
    60	case `CLAUDE.md` §8.4 covers: no hardware conclusion from a verbal description or a
    61	datasheet, on a board nobody has measured. Record the measured voltages in
    62	`docs/hardware/wiring.md` with the date.
    63	
    64	## Generated, never hand-edited
    65	
    66	`make hwdocs` regenerates these from the schematic. If a pin table and the schematic
    67	disagree, the schematic wins and the table was stale:
    68	
    69	- `docs/figures/electricalDrawing.svg` — rendered schematic, **committed**, so pull requests
    70	  show a picture instead of an S-expression diff
    71	- `docs/hardware/bom.csv` — parts list feeding `BOM.md`
    72	- `electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.net` — netlist, the source for `wiring.md` pin tables
=================== tools/README.md
     1	# tools/ — Python is allowed HERE ONLY
     2	
     3	Per the handout: the systems core is C; the interface layer may use anything, but **no
     4	graded mechanism may hide in it.** Nothing in this directory is part of the shipped
     5	product's runtime path.
     6

    10	|---|---|
    11	| `board_sync.py` | Reconciles `docs/board.toml` onto GitHub issues and the project board. Not a product tool at all — it is how the plan is maintained. See `docs/BOARD.md`. |

    21	| `plot_soak.py` | RSS / CPU / event-count series from soak heartbeats → the figure docs/EVALUATION.md §3 requires. | `plots` |
    22	
    23	**The labeling rule is absolute.** Anything these tools produce carries
    24	`src=replay` or `src=synth` in every record and every log line, all the way through to
    25	the report and the demo screen.

     1	/* obdctl — query CLI over a Unix domain socket. Shared ownership.
     2	 *
     3	 * The handout is explicit that a crisp CLI with exact semantics beats a pretty
     4	 * dashboard, and it is far more extensible at the live-modification station on demo
     5	 * day. Resist the web app.
     6	 *
     7	 * This is the ONLY directory in src/ permitted to contain network code, and only for
     8	 * the LAN interface (CLAUDE.md §2.1). `make boundary` enforces that.
     9	 */
    10	#include "common/log.h"
    11	
    12	#include <stdio.h>
    13	#include <string.h>
    14	
    15	static int usage(void)
    16	{
    17	    fputs("usage: obdctl <verb>\n"
    18	          "  status                     liveness, per-process RSS, event counts\n"
    19	          "  verdicts [--since WHEN]    current and historical diagnoses\n"
    20	          "  series PID --from --to     raw or binned history\n"
    21	          "  baseline PID               learned model for an operating-point bin\n"
    22	          "  faults                     detection / degradation / recovery events\n",
    23	          stderr);
    24	    return 2;
    25	}
    26	
    27	int main(int argc, char **argv)
    28	{
    29	    if (argc < 2) return usage();
    30	
    31	    log_init("obdctl", LOG_WARN);
    32	
    33	    static const char *verbs[] = { "status", "verdicts", "series", "baseline", "faults" };
    34	    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof verbs / sizeof verbs[0]; i++) {

    34	| **CAN** | OBD2 pin 6 / pin 14, TJA1050 transceiver, MCP2515, crystal + load caps, termination decision, `INT` to GPIO |
    35	| **Pi interface** | 40-pin header, SPI0 (CE0/MISO/MOSI/SCLK), the interrupt GPIO, grounds |
    36	| **Sensors** *(conditional, D-006)* | MPU-6050 on I2C with pull-ups; DS18B20 on 1-Wire with its 4.7 kΩ |
    37	
    38	## Rules
    39	
    40	1. **Every net that leaves a block is a named label**, not a wire crossing a boundary. The
    41	   netlist is read by humans at the defense.
    42	2. **Annotate the voltage domain on every power net** (`+12V_SW`, `+5V`, `+3V3`). The Pi has
    43	   no 5 V-tolerant inputs and no over-voltage protection; a mislabeled rail is how a Pi dies
    44	   silently in Week 13.
    45	3. **Every IC gets its decoupling drawn**, even when the module already has it. The
    46	   schematic documents what is *electrically true*, not what we happened to buy assembled.
    47	4. **The MCP2515 crystal frequency is a value field, not a comment** — 8 MHz vs 16 MHz
    48	   changes the device-tree overlay, and a wrong value produces a silently dead bus.
    49	5. **No `DNP`/`no-connect` without a reason in the field.** Floating inputs are an ERC
    50	   violation for good reasons.
    51	6. **`make hwcheck` green before the PR.** ERC violations are build failures, exactly like
    52	   `-Werror`.
    53	
    54	## What must not be trusted to a datasheet alone
    55	
    56	The cheap MCP2515 breakout modules vary: some run the TJA1050 at 5 V and level-shift the
    57	controller side, and some do not — those drive **5 V onto MISO** and will kill a Pi.
    58	
    59	**Meter it. With the Pi disconnected. Before anything is plugged in.** This is the exact
    60	case `CLAUDE.md` §8.4 covers: no hardware conclusion from a verbal description or a
    61	datasheet, on a board nobody has measured. Record the measured voltages in
    62	`docs/hardware/wiring.md` with the date.
    63	
    64	## Generated, never hand-edited
    65	
    66	`make hwdocs` regenerates these from the schematic. If a pin table and the schematic
    67	disagree, the schematic wins and the table was stale:
    68	
    69	- `docs/figures/electricalDrawing.svg` — rendered schematic, **committed**, so pull requests
    70	  show a picture instead of an S-expression diff
    71	- `docs/hardware/bom.csv` — parts list feeding `BOM.md`
    72	- `electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.net` — netlist, the source for `wiring.md` pin tables

### 4.2 Seed 1: "Is my elderly parent okay today?" (ambient wellness monitor)

The user is an adult child who lives an hour, or a continent, away from a parent who lives
alone. The moment the product exists for is a quiet one: not the fall, but the morning that
didn't follow its rhythm, noticed hours before anyone would have been frightened enough to
call. Every existing answer asks the parent to *do* something. Wear the pendant. Charge the
watch. Answer the daily check-in. And the failure mode is that the people most at risk are
precisely the people least likely to keep doing it. The design brief is then a device that
demands nothing: no camera, no microphone, no button, no new habit. That restraint is not a
limitation to apologize for. It's the product's spine, and a memo that can articulate why a
motion sensor is more respectful than a camera is a memo that understands its user.

### 4.6 Seed 5: "Ask the room" (facilities query hub)

The user is whoever answers for a room that other people complain about: the practice-space
manager, the lab steward, the roommate whose name is on the lease. The complaints arrive in
the past tense. *"It was freezing in here yesterday morning."* *"It gets stuffy every
afternoon."* And no live dashboard on earth answers a past-tense question. The product is a
**memory for a building**: several sensors, a history, and an interface that can answer
"mean CO₂ by hour, weekdays, last month" in less time than the argument takes.

**Engineering:** three or more sensors (air quality, sound level, temperature) as isolated
processes feeding a hub over IPC. That's mechanism **E**, with real supervision, since a
facilities record with a three-day hole has lost the argument it exists to win. Everything
persists through a storage layer (**D**) whose retention, rollup, and `fsync` policies you
must actually decide rather than inherit. The intelligence is the query engine: time-range
selection, aggregation, alignment of multi-rate series, and cross-sensor correlation
(afternoon CO₂ tracking the sound level is an occupancy story told by two sensors that never
met). **Where it bites:** interface ambition. Resist the pretty web app. A crisp CLI with
five query verbs and exact semantics is more defensible, and far more extensible at the
live-modification station on demo day, than a dashboard with none. This is the seed for
teams who suspect they might enjoy building databases, because it is one, in miniature,
standing on an IPC layer they also built.

minutes per team, in 3 movements.

**The demonstration.** Your device, running your soaked build, doing its job. At a moment of
our choosing, **we will inject a fault, most often by unplugging one of your sensors
mid-demo.** This is announced now so that nobody can call it unfair later. The graded
behaviors are graceful degradation, honest reporting through your own interface, and the log
line proving the system noticed. A device that freezes, lies, or crashes when hardware
misbehaves has failed its user at exactly the moment it existed for.

*"why can't this ring overwrite an unread sample?"*), one judgment call from your
`PROMPTLOG.md`, and one question from across the ownership boundary. Because owning your

    34

    45	    # an empty body, a dangling blocked_by, self-blocking, and dependency cycles.

    67	        check("blocked" not in it["labels"],

    69	        check(len(it["blocked_by"]) == len(set(it["blocked_by"])),

## The loop

1. A block sits in the **Backlog** column, labeled `question` or `decision`.
   Claude may never close those on its own.
2. Camden and Lance answer it — in the issue thread, or in a Claude Code session.
3. Claude factors the answer through the repo: `docs/DECISIONS.md` gets the
   decision, `docs/PLAN.md` and the affected docs get the consequence, and the
   one or two `[[item]]` entries the answer actually changed get updated —
   new tasks added, dead ones marked `status = "done"`, dependencies rewired.
4. `python tools/board_sync.py` pushes exactly that delta.
5. One commit contains the answer, its consequences, and the board move.

# Supported-PID survey

**Blocks D-007 and the whole of diagnostic #1. Run this before M2.**

Method: query Mode 01 PIDs `0x00`, `0x20`, `0x40`, `0x60` — each returns a 32-bit
bitmap of which PIDs in the next block the ECU supports. A $12 ELM327 does this in ten
minutes per car; no need to wait on the MCP2515 hardware.

## What we specifically need to know

| PID | Signal | Outback | Honda | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x0C | RPM | | | |
| 0x04 | Calculated load | | | |
| 0x05 | Coolant temp | | | |
| 0x0F | Intake air temp | | | |
| 0x0B | MAP | | | |
| 0x06/0x07 | Short/long term fuel trim B1 | | | |
| 0x5C | Engine oil temp | | | |
| **—** | **Oil pressure** | | | **Usually NOT a standard PID.** Check for a manufacturer-specific frame, or accept that only a binary low-pressure switch exists. |
| 0x2F | Fuel level | | | |
| 0x31 | Distance since codes cleared | | | odometer proxy for oil-age trending |

## If oil pressure is unavailable on both vehicles

Options, in order of preference:
1. Sniff manufacturer-specific frames for an analog pressure value (real work, real
   payoff, and exactly the CAN reverse-engineering this project was originally about).
2. Add a physical pressure sender with a T-fitting at the sender port. Real automotive
   work on a daily driver — do not commit to this after Week 10.
3. Replace diagnostic #1 with an oil-*temperature*-based thermal-load metric and say so
   plainly in docs/DESIGN.md §5 as a declared substitution.

Record the outcome here and update `docs/decisions/D-003-narrow-the-claim.md`.

## A.6 — Plug-in form: OBD2 port for data, car USB-C for power ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
`D-011` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** The device is a box anyone could install without tools:
- **Data:** a Y-splitter (pass-through) cable at the OBD2 port — CAN_H pin 6, CAN_L pin 14,
  signal ground pin 5 — into the MCP2515 module. The port stays usable for a scan tool
  or an emissions inspection.
- **Power:** the car's own USB-C port, or a USB-C adapter in the 12 V socket, into the Pi.
  **OBD2 pin 16 is not used.** The 12 V→5 V buck converter leaves the BOM.
- **Nothing is cut, spliced, pierced or clamped** on either car.

**Why.** The product thesis is that this is a thing an ordinary owner plugs in, so the
prototype is built the way the product would be installed. We are building the model to
prove the idea is worth something, not the finished product — but a prototype that needs
harness surgery proves a different, less interesting idea. Switched USB power also means
no battery drain while parked, and it makes mechanism D's defining constraint literally
true: power is cut, unannounced, at every key-off.

**Alternatives rejected** (discussed 2026-09-21):
- *Splice CAN_H/CAN_L behind the OBD2 port.* The wires behind the port are the same
  conductors as pins 6 and 14 — same traffic, plus a cut harness on a daily driver. If a
  gateway were filtering the port, a splice there would not get past it either.
- *In-line harness at the forward camera.* Not available: the 2015 CR-V EX-L has no Honda
  Sensing camera (D-007).
- *Contactless (inductive) CAN clamp.* Receive-only, a black box between the bus and our
  code, and it needs a wiring diagram to find the pair.
- *OBD2 pin 16 + our own buck converter.* Live with the key off (battery drain), and more
  hardware to build and defend.

**Rules this imposes** (also in `docs/hardware/wiring.md`):
1. **Remove the module's 120 Ω termination jumper.** The car's bus is already terminated;
   ours would drop it to ~40 Ω.
2. **Keep the stub short** — the Y-cable plus module leads under ~0.3 m at 500 kbit/s.
3. **The Pi must not brown out at crank.** Adapter rated ≥ 5.1 V / 3 A (Pi 4). Proven by
   `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start, not by the adapter's label.

**Cost.**
- No recording while the key is off — nothing happens then worth recording, but the device
  also cannot run overnight in a parked car.
- D-006 option (c), the parked-car soak, now requires a socket that stays live in
  accessory plus a battery tender.
- USB ground and OBD2 signal ground both reach chassis by different paths. Expected to be
  harmless; **measure before trusting it** (CLAUDE.md §8.4).
- The CAN side still needs a physical cable to the port; the product is "one box, two
  cables", not "one dongle".

## A.6 — Plug-in form: OBD2 port for data, car USB-C for power ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
`D-011` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** The device is a box anyone could install without tools:
- **Data:** a Y-splitter (pass-through) cable at the OBD2 port — CAN_H pin 6, CAN_L pin 14,
  signal ground pin 5 — into the MCP2515 module. The port stays usable for a scan tool
  or an emissions inspection.
- **Power:** the car's own USB-C port, or a USB-C adapter in the 12 V socket, into the Pi.
  **OBD2 pin 16 is not used.** The 12 V→5 V buck converter leaves the BOM.
- **Nothing is cut, spliced, pierced or clamped** on either car.

**Why.** The product thesis is that this is a thing an ordinary owner plugs in, so the
prototype is built the way the product would be installed. We are building the model to
prove the idea is worth something, not the finished product — but a prototype that needs
harness surgery proves a different, less interesting idea. Switched USB power also means
no battery drain while parked, and it makes mechanism D's defining constraint literally
true: power is cut, unannounced, at every key-off.

**Alternatives rejected** (discussed 2026-09-21):
- *Splice CAN_H/CAN_L behind the OBD2 port.* The wires behind the port are the same
  conductors as pins 6 and 14 — same traffic, plus a cut harness on a daily driver. If a
  gateway were filtering the port, a splice there would not get past it either.
- *In-line harness at the forward camera.* Not available: the 2015 CR-V EX-L has no Honda
  Sensing camera (D-007).
- *Contactless (inductive) CAN clamp.* Receive-only, a black box between the bus and our
  code, and it needs a wiring diagram to find the pair.
- *OBD2 pin 16 + our own buck converter.* Live with the key off (battery drain), and more
  hardware to build and defend.

**Rules this imposes** (also in `docs/hardware/wiring.md`):
1. **Remove the module's 120 Ω termination jumper.** The car's bus is already terminated;
   ours would drop it to ~40 Ω.
2. **Keep the stub short** — the Y-cable plus module leads under ~0.3 m at 500 kbit/s.
3. **The Pi must not brown out at crank.** Adapter rated ≥ 5.1 V / 3 A (Pi 4). Proven by
   `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start, not by the adapter's label.

**Cost.**
- No recording while the key is off — nothing happens then worth recording, but the device
  also cannot run overnight in a parked car.
- D-006 option (c), the parked-car soak, now requires a socket that stays live in
  accessory plus a battery tender.
- USB ground and OBD2 signal ground both reach chassis by different paths. Expected to be
  harmless; **measure before trusting it** (CLAUDE.md §8.4).
- The CAN side still needs a physical cable to the port; the product is "one box, two
  cables", not "one dongle".

## OBD2 connector

| OBD2 pin | Signal |
|---|---|
| 6 | CAN_H |
| 14 | CAN_L |
| 16 | +12 V battery (always live) |
| 4, 5 | Chassis / signal ground |

**Pin 16 is live with the key off.** That is what makes the unattended soak possible and
what makes a dead battery possible. Fuse it, and measure the device's key-off draw
before leaving it in a car overnight — record the number in `docs/EVALUATION.md`.
input.new_string:
## OBD2 connector — data only (D-011)

Connected through a **pass-through Y-splitter**, so the port stays free for a scan tool.
Nothing on the car is cut, spliced or pierced.

| OBD2 pin | Signal | Used? |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | CAN_H | yes → module CAN_H |
| 14 | CAN_L | yes → module CAN_L |
| 5 | Signal ground | yes → module GND (CAN reference) |
| 4 | Chassis ground | no |
| 16 | +12 V battery (always live) | **no** — power comes from USB-C, below |

**Before the module ever touches a car:**
1. **Remove the module's 120 Ω termination jumper** (often `J1`). The car's bus is already
   terminated at both ends; a third terminator drops it to ~40 Ω.
2. **Keep the stub short:** Y-cable plus module leads under ~0.3 m at 500 kbit/s.

## Power — the car's USB-C (D-011)

The Pi is powered from the car's own USB-C port, or a USB-C adapter in the 12 V socket.
There is no buck converter and no connection to OBD2 pin 16.

| Check | How | Record |
|---|---|---|
| Is the port switched (off with the key)? | Meter or a USB power tester, key off / ACC / run | here, per car |
| Does it hold the Pi up at crank? | `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start; must be `0x0` | here, per car |
| Rating | ≥ 5.1 V / 3 A for a Pi 4 | adapter model, here |
| Ground offset | Meter Pi GND to OBD2 pin 5, engine running | the reading, with the date |

A cheap built-in USB port is the likeliest silent failure in this design: an undervolted Pi
keeps running and corrupts the SD card later. Prove the port, do not trust its label.

# Wiring and electrical safety

> **The Pi's GPIO is 3.3 V and has zero over-voltage protection.** Feed a pin 5 V and
> it can die silently — sometimes taking the SoC with it. Swap VCC and GND and the
> board usually does not warn you first; it just stops working.
>
> Rules, non-negotiable: **breadboard anything 5 V-adjacent first. Check every voltage
> with a meter before the Pi is ever plugged in. Wire with the board powered off.**

## MCP2515 module → Pi

| MCP2515 | Pi pin | Pi signal | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| VCC | [TBD] | 3.3 V or 5 V | **Read your module.** Many boards run the TJA1050 transceiver at 5 V and level-shift the MCP2515 side; many cheap clones do not and will drive 5 V onto MISO. Verify before connecting. |
| GND | 6 | GND | Common ground with the vehicle. |
| CS | 24 | GPIO8 / SPI0_CE0 | |
| SO (MISO) | 21 | GPIO9 / SPI0_MISO | **Meter this line for 5 V before connecting.** |
| SI (MOSI) | 19 | GPIO10 / SPI0_MOSI | |
| SCK | 23 | GPIO11 / SPI0_SCLK | |
| INT | [TBD] | GPIO25 (proposed) | Edge-triggered. This line *is* mechanism B. |

**Crystal:** note whether your module has an 8 MHz or 16 MHz crystal — it goes straight
into the bitrate configuration and a wrong value produces a silently dead bus.

```
dtoverlay=mcp2515-can0,oscillator=<8000000|16000000>,interrupt=25
dtoverlay=spi0-hw-cs
```

## OBD2 connector

| OBD2 pin | Signal |
|---|---|
| 6 | CAN_H |
| 14 | CAN_L |
| 16 | +12 V battery (always live) |
| 4, 5 | Chassis / signal ground |

**Pin 16 is live with the key off.** That is what makes the unattended soak possible and
what makes a dead battery possible. Fuse it, and measure the device's key-off draw
before leaving it in a car overnight — record the number in `docs/EVALUATION.md`.

## Bring-up order

1. Meter the module's VCC and MISO with the Pi disconnected.
2. Pi + module on the bench, no car. `ip link show can0`.
3. Two-node bench bus (module + USB-to-CAN adapter) — prove frames move before a car is
   ever involved.
4. Car, engine off, key to accessory. `candump can0`.
5. Car, running.

Do not skip step 3. Debugging a silent bus with a car attached is debugging two
unknowns at once.
