# carwatch

An always-on in-vehicle diagnostic recorder. It reads a car's own sensors through the
OBD2 port, learns what *that specific car* looks like at each operating point, and reports
developing faults that a mileage sticker and a check-engine light both miss.

CS 370 Operating Systems term project — Camden Thomas & Lance Baron, Colorado State
University.

> **Status: M0 scaffolding.** Structure and contracts are in place; subsystems are
> stubs. See `docs/milestones.md`.

## What it does

| Diagnostic | Sensors that cooperate | Why a threshold can't do it |
|---|---|---|
| Oil pressure degradation across oil life | oil pressure + RPM + coolant temp | Oil pressure is a function of RPM and oil temperature. The signal is the *residual* after normalizing for both, trended over weeks. |
| Cooling system anomaly | coolant temp + ambient/intake temp + engine load | A short-cycling thermostat has a period and amplitude. A single temperature reading has neither. |
| Mixture drift (vacuum leak / failing O2 / dirty MAF) | short+long term fuel trim + MAP + RPM | Trim values are only meaningful relative to load; the diagnosis is which way trims move *as load changes*. |

## Hardware

See `docs/hardware/BOM.md` for the parts list and `docs/hardware/wiring.md` for the
connections and the safety notes. Summary: a Raspberry Pi 4 and a USB OBD2 adapter in
the car's OBD2 port, appearing on the Pi as `/dev/obd` (decision D-015). Power comes
from the car's USB-C port or a 12 V-socket USB-C adapter — no wiring into the car,
nothing cut (decision D-011). One LED on
GPIO17 is the warning light: slow blink = recording, double-blink = a finding, fast
blink = degraded, **steady on or off = not running** (decision D-014).

## Quick start (clean Raspberry Pi OS)

```sh
git clone <repo> && cd CS370-Term-Project
./scripts/provision_pi.sh      # packages, /dev/obd udev rule, service units
make                           # -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean
make test
sudo ./scripts/install.sh      # installs supervisor + daemons
obdctl status
```

Full TA-facing walkthrough is filled in at M4. **If the TA can't boot it, the TA can't
grade it** — this file is graded.

## Query interface

```
obdctl status                        # liveness, per-process RSS, event counts
obdctl verdicts [--since <when>]     # current and historical diagnoses
obdctl series <pid> --from --to      # raw or binned history
obdctl baseline <pid>                # the learned model for an operating-point bin
obdctl faults                        # detection/degradation/recovery events
```

**From a phone:** join the device's own Wi-Fi network (no internet — it has none) and open
its status page. The page is read-only and shows exactly `status` and `verdicts`; anything
deeper is `obdctl` (decision D-013).

## Repository layout

```
src/         systems core, C17, -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean
  common/    logging, time, config, error paths
  can/       MCP2515 SPI + interrupt RX path        [mechanism B]
  ipc/       SPSC no-drop ring, UDS protocol        [mechanisms E, F]
  store/     append-only crash-consistent log       [mechanism D]
  analysis/  features, baselines, model, state machine
  supervisor/ watchdog, restart policy              [mechanism E]
  interface/ obdctl query CLI + read-only phone status page (D-013)
tools/       PYTHON ALLOWED HERE ONLY — replay harness, training, plots,
             board_sync.py (reconciles docs/board.toml onto the GitHub board)
tests/       unit tests and fixtures
fixtures/    labeled captures, including induced faults
soak/        soak runner, heartbeat logs, fault injection
docs/        PROBLEM.md, DESIGN.md, EVALUATION.md (the three graded documents)
             board.toml (every task/question/decision) + BOARD.md (how it works)
             DECISIONS.md (audit log), PLAN.md (why the plan is shaped this way),
             milestones.md, handout/ (the rubric as markdown), hardware/
partners/    per-partner PROMPTLOG, REFLECTION, raw .jsonl transcripts
```

## The boundary

This product contains no LLM client, no cloud inference, and no third-party pretrained
model. The classifier weights in `models/` were trained by us from data we collected;
the training code is in `tools/train/`. The only network activity in the shipped tree
is serving the read-only status page on the device's own Wi-Fi access point, which has
no upstream connection. See `CLAUDE.md` §2.

# carwatch

An always-on in-vehicle diagnostic recorder. It reads a car's own sensors through the
OBD2 port, learns what *that specific car* looks like at each operating point, and reports
developing faults that a mileage sticker and a check-engine light both miss.

CS 370 Operating Systems term project — Camden Thomas & Lance Baron, Colorado State
University.

> **Status: M0 scaffolding.** Structure and contracts are in place; subsystems are
> stubs. See `docs/milestones.md`.

## What it does

| Diagnostic | Sensors that cooperate | Why a threshold can't do it |
|---|---|---|
| Oil pressure degradation across oil life | oil pressure + RPM + coolant temp | Oil pressure is a function of RPM and oil temperature. The signal is the *residual* after normalizing for both, trended over weeks. |
| Cooling system anomaly | coolant temp + ambient/intake temp + engine load | A short-cycling thermostat has a period and amplitude. A single temperature reading has neither. |
| Mixture drift (vacuum leak / failing O2 / dirty MAF) | short+long term fuel trim + MAP + RPM | Trim values are only meaningful relative to load; the diagnosis is which way trims move *as load changes*. |

## Hardware

See `docs/hardware/BOM.md` for the parts list and `docs/hardware/wiring.md` for the
connections and the safety notes. Summary: a Raspberry Pi 4 and a USB OBD2 adapter in
the car's OBD2 port, appearing on the Pi as `/dev/obd` (decision D-015). Power comes
from the car's USB-C port or a 12 V-socket USB-C adapter — no wiring into the car,
nothing cut (decision D-011). One LED on GPIO17 is the warning light: slow blink =
recording, double-blink = a finding, fast blink = degraded, **steady on or off = not
running** (decision D-014).

## Quick start (clean Raspberry Pi OS)

```sh
git clone <repo> && cd CS370-Term-Project
./scripts/provision_pi.sh      # packages, /dev/obd udev rule, service units
make                           # -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean
make test
sudo ./scripts/install.sh      # installs supervisor + daemons
obdctl status
```

Full TA-facing walkthrough is filled in at M4. **If the TA can't boot it, the TA can't
grade it** — this file is graded.

## Query interface

```
obdctl status                        # liveness, per-process RSS, event counts
obdctl verdicts [--since <when>]     # current and historical diagnoses
obdctl series <pid> --from --to      # raw or binned history
obdctl baseline <pid>                # the learned model for an operating-point bin
obdctl faults                        # detection/degradation/recovery events
```

**From a phone:** join the device's own Wi-Fi network (no internet — it has none) and open
its status page. The page is read-only and shows exactly `status` and `verdicts`; anything
deeper is `obdctl` (decision D-013).

## Repository layout

```
src/                systems core, C17, -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean
  can/              capture daemon: Mode 01 requests over the OBD2 adapter tty
  ipc/              SPSC ring + Unix-socket protocol between processes   [mechanism E]
  store/            append-only crash-consistent log                     [mechanism D]
  analysis/         binning, baselines, residuals, trends, model, state machine
  supervisor/       spawn, restart with backoff, heartbeats, warning light [mechanism E]
  interface/        obdctl CLI + read-only phone status page (D-013)
  common/           logging and shared helpers
include/            headers, one directory per src/ subsystem
tests/              unit tests (make test)
tools/              Python only here: board sync, PID scan, replay, training
scripts/            provision a clean Pi; install the service
soak/               48-hour soak runner and fault injection
docs/               everything written — start at docs/README.md
electricalDrawing/  KiCad schematic (Lance)
partners/           each partner's PROMPTLOG, REFLECTION, raw transcripts
```

Created when their first file lands, not before: `fixtures/` (labeled captures),
`models/` (our weights), `build/` and `soak/logs/` (both git-ignored).

## The boundary

This product contains no LLM client, no cloud inference, and no third-party pretrained
model. The classifier weights in `models/` were trained by us from data we collected;
the training code is in `tools/train/`. The only network activity in the shipped tree
is serving the read-only status page on the device's own Wi-Fi access point, which has
no upstream connection. See `CLAUDE.md` §2.

1	# carwatch
2	
3	An always-on in-vehicle diagnostic recorder. It reads a car's own sensors through the
4	OBD2 port, learns what *that specific car* looks like at each operating point, and reports
5	developing faults that a mileage sticker and a check-engine light both miss.
6	
7	CS 370 Operating Systems term project — Camden Thomas & Lance Baron, Colorado State
8	University.
9	
10	> **Status: M1.** Structure and contracts are in place; subsystems are stubs. Every
11	> document is indexed in [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md); progress is in
12	> [`docs/milestones.md`](docs/milestones.md).
13	
14	## What it does
15	
16	| Diagnostic | Sensors that cooperate | Why a threshold can't do it |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| Oil pressure degradation across oil life | oil pressure + RPM + coolant temp | Oil pressure is a function of RPM and oil temperature. The signal is the *residual* after normalizing for both, trended over weeks. |
19	| Cooling system anomaly | coolant temp + ambient/intake temp + engine load | A short-cycling thermostat has a period and amplitude. A single temperature reading has neither. |
20	| Mixture drift (vacuum leak / failing O2 / dirty MAF) | short+long term fuel trim + MAP + RPM | Trim values are only meaningful relative to load; the diagnosis is which way trims move *as load changes*. |
21	
22	## Hardware
23	
24	See `docs/hardware/BOM.md` for the parts list and `docs/hardware/wiring.md` for the
25	connections and the safety notes. Summary: a Raspberry Pi 4 and a USB OBD2 adapter in
26	the car's OBD2 port, appearing on the Pi as `/dev/obd` (decision D-015). Power comes
27	from the car's USB-C port or a 12 V-socket USB-C adapter — no wiring into the car,
28	nothing cut (decision D-011). One LED on GPIO17 is the warning light: slow blink =
29	recording, double-blink = a finding, fast blink = degraded, **steady on or off = not
30	running** (decision D-014).
31	
32	## Quick start (clean Raspberry Pi OS)
33	
34	```sh
35	git clone <repo> && cd CS370-Term-Project
36	./scripts/provision_pi.sh      # packages, /dev/obd udev rule, service units
37	make                           # -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean
38	make test
39	sudo ./scripts/install.sh      # installs supervisor + daemons
40	obdctl status
41	```
42	
43	Full TA-facing walkthrough is filled in at M4. **If the TA can't boot it, the TA can't
44	grade it** — this file is graded.
45	
46	## Query interface
47	
48	```
49	obdctl status                        # liveness, per-process RSS, event counts
50	obdctl verdicts [--since <when>]     # current and historical diagnoses
51	obdctl series <pid> --from --to      # raw or binned history
52	obdctl baseline <pid>                # the learned model for an operating-point bin
53	obdctl faults                        # detection/degradation/recovery events
54	```
55	
56	**From a phone:** join the device's own Wi-Fi network (no internet — it has none) and open
57	its status page. The page is read-only and shows exactly `status` and `verdicts`; anything
58	deeper is `obdctl` (decision D-013).
59	
60	## Repository layout
61	
62	```
63	src/                systems core, C17, -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean
64	  obd/              capture daemon: Mode 01 requests over the OBD2 adapter tty
65	  ipc/              SPSC ring + Unix-socket protocol between processes   [mechanism E]
66	  store/            append-only crash-consistent log                     [mechanism D]
67	  analysis/         binning, baselines, residuals, trends, model, state machine
68	  supervisor/       spawn, restart with backoff, heartbeats, warning light [mechanism E]
69	  interface/        obdctl CLI + read-only phone status page (D-013)
70	  common/           logging and shared helpers
71	include/            headers, one directory per src/ subsystem
72	tests/              unit tests (make test)
73	tools/              Python only here: board sync, PID scan, replay, training
74	scripts/            provision a clean Pi; install the service
75	soak/               48-hour soak runner and fault injection
76	docs/               everything written — start at docs/README.md
77	electricalDrawing/  KiCad schematic (Lance)
78	partners/           each partner's PROMPTLOG, REFLECTION, raw transcripts
79	```
80	
81	Created when their first file lands, not before: `fixtures/` (labeled captures),
82	`models/` (our weights), `build/` and `soak/logs/` (both git-ignored).
83	
84	## The boundary
85	
86	This product contains no LLM client, no cloud inference, and no third-party pretrained
87	model. The classifier weights in `models/` were trained by us from data we collected;
88	the training code is in `tools/train/`. The only network activity in the shipped tree
89	is serving the read-only status page on the device's own Wi-Fi access point, which has
90	no upstream connection. See `CLAUDE.md` §2.

│ (D-015)      │  [N] baud           │  tty reader    │  [N] req/s, round-robin (D-012)
│ SPSC ring, [N] samples/s  (mech F only with pisensor)

-- [ ] `candaemon` → ring → `storaged` → disk, end to end, on a real car
+- [ ] `obdd` → ring → `storaged` → disk, end to end, on a real car

> **Stacked on #83.** The base is `camden/m1/product-topology`, so this diff shows only this PR's commits. Merge #83 first. PR B (the C rename) is stacked on this one. ## What this changes It brings the repository in line with Camden's M1 memo and his answers on 2026-09-21: - **Data path:** the Pi reads the car through a **USB OBD2 adapter**. Raw CAN becomes a stretch goal. - **Testbed:** one car, **Lance's 2015 CR-V**. - **Mechanisms:** **D and E** are committed. B and F come back only if the Pi gets its own sensor. - **Soak:** the question is reframed around the **fake OBD2 port** from the memo. It also removes stale information and empty placeholder directories everywhere, and adds `docs/README.md` as a one-page index of every document. Docs, board, one shell script and one Python docstring. **No C.** ## Why **Decision IDs touched:** - **New:** D-015, D-016, D-017, all ⚠️ UNREVIEWED. - **Superseded, moved to §G:** D-001, D-005, D-002. - **Revised in place:** D-011 and D-012. Both are unreviewed in #83, so no human has treated them as binding yet. - **Reframed:** D-006. **Answered:** D-008. **Milestone:** M1 **Mechanism affected (B / D / E / F / none):** all four. D and E are committed. B and F are conditional on the new decision item `pisensor`. Closes: board item `overhaul`. The issue number will exist after the next `board_sync.py` run. ## Review this hardest 1. **D-017's mechanism loss.** Handout §3.2 defines B as an interrupt *our design* services and F as a *high-rate* stream. A USB adapter at about 10–20 replies/s gives neither, so only D and E stand. That's the floor with nothing in reserve. `pisensor` (an MPU-6050 and/or DS18B20, about $8) is the recovery, and my recommendation is **both**. 2. **Handout §3.1, two physically distinct sensors.** The car's sensors are distinct, but they all arrive through one USB device. A grader could call that one sensor. This risk is written into `pisensor`. 3. **The `obdsim` training caution.** The memo proposes training the model on the fake port. The item body argues against that: a model trained on our generator learns the generator. Camden, decide whether you agree. 4. **The thesis change (CLAUDE.md §3, D-016).** "Two cars with the same sticker disagree" becomes "this car's measured condition against its own sticker and its own Maintenance Minder." ## What I am least sure about - **Whether this is one claim.** I kept it as one PR because every decision edits the same Review Queue table, CLAUDE.md §3 and a dozen shared tables, so separate PRs would conflict with each other. Each decision is still its own commit and reverts cleanly. **Lance, if you would approve some and not others, say which and I'll split along those lines.** - **Editing LOCKED E.1 and F.1 in place** (a one-line note each) rather than moving them to §G, because only a vehicle count and a superseded line cap changed. Say if you'd rather they be superseded outright. - **The adapter numbers** (about 10–20 replies/s, 115200 vs 38400 baud) are typical figures, not measurements. `bench` records the real ones. ## Commit-by-commit 1. `4440427` Camden's PROBLEM.md draft, as he wrote it. 2. `6e4bfd2` Camden's M0 check-offs in milestones.md. 3. `35cf0ad` Camden's PROMPTLOG E-02. 4. `e18ddea` **D-015:** USB OBD2 adapter; raw CAN is a stretch goal. Wiring, BOM, PID survey, DESIGN, PLAN, provisioning, board. 5. `8cd4bac` **D-016:** the CR-V is the only testbed; the E.1 claim is narrowed. 6. `c573c6a` **D-017:** mechanisms D + E; B and F conditional. New items `pisensor` and `expkill`. 7. `7e8e18f` Fix-up: D-016 missed a DESIGN §5 row. 8. `7e72543` **D-006:** reframed around the fake OBD2 port. The email moves into `soakq`; new item `obdsim`. 9. `61d1f77` Records Camden's check-offs: D-008 dates verified, `cleanup` done. 10. `072351d` The commit template, PR template and F.1 now match CLAUDE.md §7.3. Deletes the obsolete template note. 11. `1e20c86` Removes all 7 `.gitkeep` files and `src/capture/`, plus every reference to them. 12. `be0c382` Adds `docs/README.md` (the index); the README layout now matches the tree. 13. `e7a8a39` Fix-up: `oilq` still said "sniff CAN frames". 14. `645ffaa` Board item `overhaul`, which traces this PR. 15. `4cc746b` The README describes `include/` accurately. The two fix-ups are separate commits so the misses stay visible; they weren't folded back into the originals. ## Verification — paste real output, do not summarize
make ``` $ make /usr/bin/bash: line 1: make: command not found ```
make test ``` $ make test /usr/bin/bash: line 1: make: command not found $ python tools/test_board.py # the board half of make test board.toml PASS (88 items, 7 milestones) ```
make asan ``` $ make asan /usr/bin/bash: line 1: make: command not found ```
This machine has no gcc, make or WSL. **This PR changes no C and no Makefile**, so `make` and `make asan` can't be affected by it. The board half of `make test` passes, as shown above. Other checks: - `git ls-files | grep -c gitkeep` returns `0`. - A stale-term sweep (`MCP2515|SPI|candump|SocketCAN|Subaru|Outback|drivers/|src/capture|cangen`) finds only intentional hits: superseded decisions in §G, cut notes, the stretch-goal BOM table, and Lance's KiCad docs. - `python tools/board_sync.py --check --no-board`: 8 issues to create, about 40 bodies or titles to update, `cleanup` to close. - Three cut items, `twonode`, `meterv` and `pidsub`, are labeled `hardware`. **A human must close them with `--close-questions`.** ## Not touched, for Lance `electricalDrawing/`, D-009/D-010, `schematic-conventions.md` and the `sch*` board items still describe the MCP2515 schematic. Only one line of `schematic-conventions.md` changed, because it cited `src/capture/`. Whether KiCad stays in the project now that the electronics are an off-the-shelf adapter plus one LED is Lance's call. content.text:
The overhaul is done and split into two draft PRs stacked on #83. One thing is unverified: this machine has no gcc, make or WSL, so the C rename in #85 has not been compiled. The board check (`test_board.py`) passes, and the GitHub issues are synced with no drift remaining.

## What changed

- **Data path (D-015):** the Pi reads the car through a USB OBD2 adapter showing up as `/dev/obd`. Raw CAN is now a stretch goal only; it survives only as "stretch" and in the superseded-decisions section. Wiring, parts list, PID survey, design doc, plan, provisioning script and board were all rewritten to match.
- **One car (D-016):** the Outback is gone everywhere. The claim is narrowed to "this vehicle". The pitch changes from "two cars with the same sticker disagree" to "this car measured against its own sticker and its own Maintenance Minder".
- **Mechanisms (D-017):** this corrects what I told you in the question. We commit to D and E only. Mode 01 at 10–20 replies/s gives B no interrupt of ours and gives F no real rate, so both come back only with a sensor on the Pi itself (new decision item `pisensor`). I added `expkill`, since mechanism E had no experiment of its own.
- **Soak (D-006):** reframed around your fake OBD2 port. The professor email now lives in the `soakq` item, and `obdsim` (a software fake port, all output labeled synth) is a new task.
- **File system:**
  - All 7 placeholder files and `src/capture/` are deleted.
  - The old line-count rules are removed from the commit and PR templates.
  - `src/can/` is now `src/obd/` and `candaemon` is now `obdd` (that's #85).
  - `docs/README.md` is a new one-page index of every document.

PRs, to be merged in order:
- [#83](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/83), closes #86
- [#84](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/84), 17 commits, closes #87
- [#85](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/85), 4 commits, part of #87

## Needs you

- **Decide `pisensor` (#93).** It settles the mechanism count, the "two physically distinct sensors" rule, and a live soak all at once. I recommend adding both sensors, about $8.
- **Close the cut items.** Run `python tools/board_sync.py --close-questions --no-board` for #11, #19 and #33, then close #6. Mark D-008 LOCKED in your own commit.
- **Fix `gh` scopes.** Run `gh auth refresh -s project`. Until then the project-board half of the sync can't run.
- **Build #85.** Run `make && make test && make asan` on the Pi and paste the output before it leaves draft.
- **Lance should review** D-007 and D-011 through D-017, and decide whether KiCad stays now that the electronics are an off-the-shelf adapter plus one LED. His schematic files are still MCP2515-era; I left them alone.

## Your PROBLEM.md

I only replaced the stale MCP2515 mechanisms paragraph. Your own prose has four problems before it's submitted:
- **The user section is a persona.** "The typical American" gets returned under the rubric. Name the person who drives the CR-V.
- **"Predict failures"** contradicts the claim you're defending: detecting three induced faults, with measured error rates.
- **The risk section proposes training the model on the fake port.** The `obdsim` item argues against that: a model trained on our generator learns the generator, not the car.
- **Typos:** releying, thier, vihicle/vihivles, viriaty, undestand, getiing, viscosisty, worl.

When the sync regenerated the milestones table, it reverted your formatting inside the generated section. Style changes there have to go into `board_sync.py`.
